question: Mean of the values 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 is:
explanation:
• Mean = (10+20+30+40+50)/5 = 150/5 = 30.
• Mean is the average; sensitive to outliers.

question: In research, the independent variable is:
options: B. The variable that is manipulated or varied
C. Always the same in all groups
explanation:
• Independent variable: manipulated by researcher (e.g. treatment vs control).
• Dependent variable: outcome measured.

question: Probability sampling method where every member has equal chance:
explanation:
• Simple random: each member of population has equal probability of selection.
• Reduces selection bias.

question: Median of 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 is:
explanation:
• Median = middle value when ordered. Here 3,5,7,9,11 → median = 7.
• Used when data is skewed.

question: Autocratic leadership is characterized by:
options: B. Leader makes decisions without much input
explanation:
• Autocratic: leader decides alone, minimal subordinate input.
• Democratic: participative; Laissez-faire: minimal leader direction.

question: First step in nursing research process is:
explanation:
• Research process: identify problem, review literature, design, collect data, analyze, disseminate.
• Problem identification is the first step.

question: Mode is the value that:
explanation:
• Mode = most frequently occurring value.
• Useful for categorical data.

question: Inventory management in hospital includes:
options: B. Stock control, ordering, storage, expiry tracking
explanation:
• Inventory: maintaining stock, reorder levels, storage conditions, expiry, minimizing wastage.
• Critical for drugs and supplies.

question: Qualitative research often uses:
explanation:
• Qualitative: interviews, focus groups, observation, content analysis—explores meaning and context.
• Quantitative: numbers and statistics.

question: Span of control refers to:
options: B. Number of subordinates a manager supervises
explanation:
• Span of control: number of subordinates reporting to one supervisor.
• Wide span = many subordinates; narrow = fewer.

question: Stratified sampling:
options: B. Population divided into strata; sample from each stratum
explanation:
• Stratified: divide population into strata (e.g. age groups); sample from each.
• Ensures representation of subgroups.

question: Null hypothesis in research:
options: B. Statement of no difference/no effect (to be tested)
explanation:
• Null (H0): no difference/effect. Alternative (H1): there is difference/effect.
• Statistical test rejects or fails to reject H0.

question: Democratic leadership:
options: B. Participative; involves team in decisions
explanation:
• Democratic: leader involves subordinates in decision-making; consultation.
• Can improve morale and ownership.

question: Standard deviation measures:
options: B. Spread or dispersion of data around mean
explanation:
• SD: measure of spread. High SD = more dispersion. Low SD = data clustered near mean.
• Variance = SD².

question: Ward management includes:
options: B. Staffing, supplies, safety, cleanliness, coordination
explanation:
• Ward management: staffing, supplies, infection control, safety, coordination with other departments.
• Nurse manager role.

question: Cross-sectional study:
options: B. Data collected at one point in time from different subjects
explanation:
• Cross-sectional: snapshot at one time. Longitudinal: same subjects over time.
• Prevalence studies often cross-sectional.

question: Quality assurance in nursing:
options: B. Systematic evaluation to ensure standards are met
explanation:
• QA: monitor and evaluate care against standards; improve processes.
• Audits, indicators, feedback.

question: Informed consent in research:
options: B. Participant must understand and voluntarily agree
explanation:
• Informed consent: full disclosure, understanding, voluntary agreement. Ethical requirement.
• Written consent; can withdraw.

question: Laissez-faire leadership:
options: B. Minimal leader direction; group has freedom
explanation:
• Laissez-faire: leader provides little direction; group decides. Can work with motivated experts.
• May lead to chaos if group needs structure.
